name: Moong Dal Chilla
ingredients: 1 cup (200 g) split yellow moong dal
Oil for the pan, about 1 tsp per chilla
steps: Rinse the dal 2-3 times, cover with plenty of water and soak for 3-4 hours. Drain well.
Blend the dal with cumin, chilli, ginger, salt and the water into a thick but pourable batter.
Stir in the onion, carrot, coriander, ajwain and turmeric.
Heat a cast-iron or non-stick pan on medium. Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it into a 6-7 inch round.
Drizzle oil around the edge, cook until golden, flip and cook the other side. Makes 8; serve 2 per person.
photoCredit: NAVYA · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Vegetable Poha
ingredients: 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (peas, diced carrot, capsicum)
steps: Rinse the poha briefly in a colander, drain and leave covered for 5 minutes to soften. Mix in salt and sugar.
Fry the peanuts in the oil until golden and crunchy; lift out and keep aside.
In the same oil crackle the mustard and cumin seeds, then add onion, curry leaves and chillies. Saute until pink.
Add the mixed vegetables, cover and cook on low for 4-5 minutes until just tender.
Stir in the turmeric and poha, cover and steam on low for 2-3 minutes. Sprinkle a little water if it looks dry.
Turn off the heat, mix in the lemon juice and top with coriander and the roasted peanuts.
photoCredit: Ajay Suresh · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Masala Oats
steps: Heat the ghee, add cumin seeds, then soften the onion and chilli. Add the ginger and garlic for a minute.
Add the tomato and cook until soft, then stir in the chilli powder, turmeric and garam masala.
Add the carrot, beans, peas and corn and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer until the vegetables are almost tender.
Stir in the oats and salt and cook uncovered, stirring, until thick but still pourable. Add hot water if needed.
Rest for a minute, then stir in the lemon juice and garnish with coriander.
photoCredit: Dr. Raju Kasambe · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Egg Bhurji
steps: Whisk the eggs with the salt and turmeric until frothy.
Heat the oil, let the cumin sizzle, then fry the onion and chilli until golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste for a minute.
Add the tomato and cook until soft and pulpy.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently over medium heat until almost set.
Sprinkle in garam masala and chilli powder and cook 1-2 minutes more. Finish with coriander; serve with roti or toast.
photoCredit: Praveen · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Strawberry Overnight Oats
steps: Put the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, honey and cinnamon into a half-pint jar with a lid.
Close the jar and shake until everything is evenly combined.
Fold in the strawberries, cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight. Eat cold.
photoCredit: Vegan Feast Catering · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Veggie Egg-White Omelette
ingredients: 3/4 cup liquid egg whites (whites of 5-6 large eggs)
2 tbsp grated cheese of your choice
steps: Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Soften the onion and pepper, then wilt in the spinach. Season.
Pour the egg whites over the vegetables. As the edges set, lift them so the runny egg flows underneath.
When just set, scatter the cheese and basil over one half, fold the omelette over and slide onto a plate.
photoCredit: Armando Olivo Martín del Campo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Rajma Masala
ingredients: 1 cup (200 g) dried rajma (red kidney beans)
steps: Soak the rajma in 4 cups of water for 8 hours or overnight, then drain and rinse.
Pressure cook with 1 1/2 cups fresh water for 4-5 whistles until fully soft. Undercooked kidney beans are unsafe.
Heat the oil, add bay leaf and cumin, then fry the onion and chilli until golden. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomato puree and cook until thick, then add the spice powders (half the garam masala) for 2-3 minutes.
Add the beans with their liquid and 1/2-1 cup hot water. Simmer for 10-15 minutes until thick and creamy.
Season with salt, the rest of the garam masala and crushed kasuri methi. Garnish with coriander; serve with rice.
photoCredit: Scott Veg · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Masoor Dal
ingredients: 1/2 cup (95 g) masoor dal (split red lentils)
steps: Wash both dals until the water runs clear. Add the tomatoes, green chilli and water.
Pressure cook for 1-2 whistles, or simmer in a covered pot until soft, skimming off froth. Mash to your liking.
For the tadka, heat the ghee and fry the mustard, cumin, dried chilli and garlic until the garlic is light golden.
Off the heat, add the chilli powder, turmeric and garam masala, then pour the tadka straight into the dal.
Add salt and crushed kasuri methi and simmer for 2 minutes. Finish with lemon juice and coriander.
photoCredit: Atudu · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Boiled Egg Kachumber Salad
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for about 10 minutes, cool them in cold water, then peel and quarter lengthwise.
Toss the tomato, onion, radish and cucumber with the vinegar, lime juice, chaat masala, chilli and half the salt.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and stir in the coriander, garlic paste, paprika, cumin and remaining salt.
Add the egg quarters and turn them gently until coated in the spices. Let them cool a little.
Pile the salad on a plate, arrange the masala eggs on top and finish with garam masala and coriander.
photoCredit: Keka De · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Grilled Chicken Salad with Harissa Yogurt
ingredients: 1 can (390 g) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Pat the chickpeas dry and brown them in the oil in a hot pan for 4-5 minutes. Season, set aside and wipe the pan.
Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thin steaks and toss with the garlic, salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken in the hot pan or a griddle over medium-high heat for 3-5 minutes a side until cooked through. Rest it.
Toss the cucumber, slaw, spinach and chickpeas with the harissa and yogurt.
Chop the chicken, toss it in its resting juices and pile it on top of the salad.
photoCredit: PattayaPatrol · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Black Bean Quinoa Bowl
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups canned low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it, covered, in the water for about 15 minutes until absorbed. Fluff and cool.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, mustard, garlic, coriander, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Divide the quinoa, beans, tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, spinach and onion among 4 bowls or jars.
Spoon the dressing over each and toss before eating. Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 4 days.
photoCredit: Joey Doll · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Mediterranean Tuna Wrap
ingredients: 2 cans (170 g each) chunk light tuna in water, well drained
steps: Mix the tuna, onion, parsley and olives in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Toss two-thirds with the tuna and the rest with the greens.
Spread a quarter of the tuna over each wrap and top with about 1 1/2 cups of greens and a few tomato slices.
Roll up tightly, cut in half and serve.
photoCredit: Jen Arrr · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Palak Paneer
steps: Saute the chillies, cashews and spinach in a little of the oil until the leaves wilt. Cool, then blend with 1/4 cup water.
Heat the remaining oil and fry the onion until golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook until fragrant.
Add the tomato and salt and cook until mushy, then stir in the garam masala.
Pour in 3/4 cup water, cover and simmer until the onion is completely soft.
Lower the heat, add the kasuri methi and spinach puree and simmer for 2-3 minutes until it just bubbles.
Fold in the paneer, warm through and swirl in the cream before serving.
photoCredit: DreamyFlutura11 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Paneer Tikka
ingredients: 1 large onion, cut into chunks and separated
6 tbsp thick Greek yogurt or hung curd
steps: Whisk the yogurt, oil, ginger-garlic paste, spices and salt into a thick marinade.
Fold in the paneer, onion and capsicum until well coated. Cover and refrigerate for 1-2 hours.
Heat the oven to 230C (450F). Thread paneer and vegetables onto oiled skewers and lay them on a lined tray.
Bake for 10-11 minutes, brushing with the leftover marinade halfway through.
Broil on the top rack for 2-3 minutes until lightly charred. Serve hot with mint chutney and lemon.
photoCredit: PallaviKhale · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Tandoori Chicken
ingredients: 750 g skinless bone-in chicken legs or thighs (4 pieces)
1/2 cup thick Greek yogurt or hung curd
steps: Cut deep slashes into the chicken. Mix everything except the coriander leaves into a thick marinade.
Rub the marinade well into the chicken, cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Heat the oven to 240C (470F). Set the chicken, spaced apart, on a greased rack over a foil-lined tray.
Roast for 15 minutes, baste with the leftover marinade, turn the pieces and roast 12-15 minutes more.
Broil for 3-4 minutes until charred and the thickest part reads 75C (165F). Garnish with coriander.
photoCredit: Bharat Mirchandani · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Light Bengali Chicken Curry
ingredients: 500 g skinless chicken pieces, on the bone
3 cloves, 3 cardamom pods, 2 cinnamon sticks, 3 bay leaves
300 g basmati rice, cooked, to serve
steps: Coat the chicken with the pureed onion, garlic, ginger, 1 tsp chilli powder and the garam masala. Set aside.
Heat the oil and fry the cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaves for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the sliced onions and cumin seeds and stir-fry over high heat for about 10 minutes until golden.
Stir in the turmeric, paprika, any extra chilli and the chicken, and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add the hot water, cover and simmer on medium for 20 minutes. Cook the rice meanwhile.
Add the peppers, cover and cook 5-10 minutes until tender and the chicken is cooked through. Serve with the rice.
photoCredit: ArghyadeepDas · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Moong Dal Khichdi
steps: Rinse the rice and dal together three times and drain.
Heat 1 1/2 tbsp ghee in a pressure cooker. Add the bay leaf and cumin, then the ginger, onion and chilli; fry until golden.
Add the tomato, turmeric and salt and cook for 3-4 minutes. Stir in the rice and dal and saute for 3 minutes.
Pour in the water, stir and cook on medium for 4-5 whistles for a soft, porridge-like khichdi.
Let the pressure drop on its own. Stir, loosen with hot water if needed and top with the remaining ghee.
photoCredit: RohitValecha · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Tofu Stir-Fry
ingredients: 450 g extra-firm tofu, drained and cut into 2.5 cm cubes
steps: Toss the tofu with the dressing and marinate for 30 minutes. Drain, keeping the marinade.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the tofu for 7-8 minutes until golden.
Add the broccoli and mushrooms for 3-4 minutes, then the spring onions and almonds for 2 minutes more.
Whisk the broth, cornstarch, soy sauce, hot sauce, sweetener, garlic and saved marinade, and pour into the wok.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes until glossy. Eat as is or over brown rice (rice not counted).
photoCredit: NeoBatfreak · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Kala Chana Chaat
steps: Rinse the kala chana and soak in about 3 cups of water for 8 hours or overnight.
Drain, then pressure cook in fresh water for 7-8 whistles (or 25 minutes in an Instant Pot) until soft but whole.
Drain the chickpeas well and tip them into a large bowl.
Add the tomato, onion, green chilli, coriander and mint.
Sprinkle over all the spices and salt, squeeze in the lemon juice, toss well and serve.
photoCredit: SamunderSinghBohriya · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Moong Sprouts Salad
ingredients: 1 small green chilli, deseeded and chopped
steps: If the sprouts are store-bought, blanch them in boiling water for a minute, then drain and rinse.
Finely chop the onion, tomato, cucumber, chilli and coriander, and grate the carrot.
Toss everything in a bowl with the salt, chaat masala and lemon juice and eat straight away.
photoCredit: Ravi Talwar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Greek Yogurt Blueberry Bowl
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Scatter the blueberries over the top.
Sprinkle with the ground flaxseed, stir through and eat straight away.
photoCredit: Missvain · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

name: Peanut Butter Banana Protein Smoothie
steps: Put the yogurt, milk, bananas, peanut butter, honey and ice into a blender.
Blend on high for about 45 seconds until completely smooth.
Pour into two glasses and drink right away.
photoCredit: Kari Sullivan · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons
